$$

Find the inverse of the following matrix:

A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]

{P}^{-1}={P}^{T}

\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]

- all entries on the main diagonal are ones

- the matrix has only one column (the $1$st column) where some entries below the main diagonal are not zeros

- all the other entries outside the main diagonal are zeros

To find the inverse of a Frobenius matrix, we simply take the non-zero entries outside the main diagonal with opposite signs. 

In our case, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

question.knowledge_point: Identifying a True Statement Concerning a 2x2 System of Equations
question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations given by

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x+\sqrt{7}y=0.3 \\ -2\sqrt{0.1}x+3y=\sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the system has exactly one solution, which of the following statements are true?

I. The lines $3x+\sqrt{7}y=0.3$ and $-2\sqrt{0.1}x+3y=\sqrt{7}$ intersect exactly at one point

II. The determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $0$

III. The coefficient matrix is invertible
question.worked_solution:
Recall that given $A=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}]$, then according to the invertible matrix theorem the following statements are equivalent:    

1\. $A$ is invertible.

2\. The system $Ax=b$ has exactly one solution for any $2\times 1$ column vector $b.$

3\. The system $Ax=0$ has the unique zero solution.

4\. The lines ${a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1}$ and ${a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2}$ intersect at exactly one point.

5\. $det(A)\ne 0.$

Also, we are told that the second part of the invertible matrix theorem is true. So, all the other parts of the theorem are true too. Therefore, according to the theorem:

- Statement I is true by the fourth part of the invertible matrix theorem.

- Statement II is false. According to the fifth part of the invertible matrix theorem, the determinant cannot be $0.$

- Statement III is true by the first part of the invertible matrix theorem.

Therefore, only statements I and III are true.

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, only statements I and III are true.
